summary: We develop Lunar Mission Planner which is a web-based decision-support tool to compare lunar landing sites and mission dates. It addresses the challenge of complicated and scattered lunar landing-site planning by bringing important mission-planning information into one web-based dashboard. It is important because it helps make lunar exploration more organized, efficient, and reliable.
details:
The Lunar Mission Planner is a web-based decision-support application designed to help users compare potential lunar landing sites and identify suitable mission dates. It analyzes important factors such as Sun elevation, Sun azimuth, Earth visibility, solar-panel power generation, and communication opportunities.

The project allows users to select predefined lunar landing sites or enter custom coordinates, choose a mission date and time, and review the calculated results through a visual dashboard. It also provides side-by-side comparisons of different landing locations to help identify promising mission windows.

The main benefits of this project are improved mission planning, easier comparison of lunar locations, better understanding of sunlight availability, and early assessment of communication opportunities. Its intended impact is to support astronauts, researchers, educators, and future lunar exploration missions with a clearer and more organized planning process.

The project uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend, Python and Flask for the application backend, and mathematical geometry models for analyzing the positions of the Sun and Earth. NASA/JPL SPICE is identified as a future integration for improving scientific accuracy.

The creative aspect of the project is bringing multiple lunar mission-planning factors together in one interactive workspace instead of requiring users to consult separate tools. Important considerations include solar energy availability, Earth visibility, communication opportunities, landing-site conditions, calculation accuracy, and future scalability.

This project provides an expandable foundation for lunar exploration planning while recognizing that its current simplified calculations require further scientific validation before real mission use.
